cmm_issue3.body:
The initial CMMMech audit found fleet admission, canonical shared curation history, vendored governance, PR shepherd deployment and native merge queue configuration pending. PR #1 establishes the scientific corpus and local review process; its Markdown reviews do not implement canonical curation history.

Evidence: [dated integration audit](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CMMMech/blob/2961df4540675b2d07aa7aa658776d779233d6c3/docs/integration-status.md). The audit distinguishes verified repository state from unknown App/credential readiness and includes hidden and ignored local files in absence checks.

Follow CLAW's supported [onboard-mech process](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw/blob/20aae24502ad6a76a1a2c6cdb1eb0d5c8ce42838/.claude/skills/onboard-mech/SKILL.md); re-read the current authority before execution. Use clean isolated worktrees and preserve the dirty local CLAW checkout.

Acceptance criteria, in dependency order:

- Reverify committed candidate and authority revisions. Register CMMMech in the fleet/configuration, consumer manifest, research enum and queue-policy contracts, with measured capability declarations and serialization round trips.
- Record only measured outstanding artifact paths in CLAW's supported incomplete-consumer ledger when needed; remove the entry on completion.
- Adopt canonical shared/history schemas through the supported governed release. Implement CMMMech-owned history adapters, `just new-history`, provenance-preserving record history and meaningful gate tests.
- Publish an immutable canonical release and coordinate synchronization/re-pinning of every consumer derived from its manifest. Run consumer checks and fleet audit at the same authority revision. Do not hand-copy governed artifacts or invent a pin.
- Verify PR shepherd App/configuration readiness without exposing credentials.
- Retain reviewed queue plan, authorized apply receipt and successful configuration check. Prove one reviewed PR merges through a real native merge group, recording reviewed head, merge-group SHA, Actions run and merge commit.

This is follow-up integration work, not a blocker for the first scientifically reviewed local corpus. Enabling a workflow trigger alone does not satisfy queue deployment. Cross-repository releases and settings changes must be handled in that integration's authorized scope.
